main_text.p: xiùs explicare non eft neceffe. Qui igitur ad oculum tactumque demon-stratum fuit, dari effervescentiam in Intestinis ab adversa acrimonia acidi & bilis ortam. Quia acidus Succus Pancreaticus frigore æstum bilis tem-perat, bilis verò caloris & æstûs caussa est, atque pituita pro ratione diversi-tatis temperamenti vel acrimoniæ utriusque temperat, vel etiam alterum alterumve adjuvat, facilè concipitur pro ratione copiæ aut acrimoniæ majoris vel minoris cujusque humoris illius Triumviratûs necessariò oriri debere effervescentiam vel naturalem moderatam, temperatam & blandam vel præternaturalem calidiorem, frigidiorem, vehementiorem, majorem diuturniorem vel contrà.
Ut falsi crimen evadere non possit, dum ait pag. 19. Sylvium Succum Pancreaticum semper pro ἰχυρῷ &τῳ, vehementissimo venditare, cujus exemplum in corrodente spiritu vitrioli aut Nitri con-

page.notes: The right portion of each line is cut off by the scan edge; the Greek word "ἰχυρῷ" is a reading of a damaged passage and uncertain. The final line "con-" is a catchword-like fragment at the right edge and is treated as the start of the next line.
